title: Application of Integrals: Area under Curves, Circles and Ellipses
seo_title: Application of Integrals Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 8)
standard_text: Applications in finding the area under simple curves, especially lines, circles, parabolas and ellipses (in standard form only) (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Application of Integrals worksheet (NCERT Chapter 8): area under lines and parabolas, circles, ellipses, areas cut by a line and areas between curves. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Area = ∫ₐᵇ y dx, taken as positive.
body_html:
How it works

  • The area between y = f(x), the x-axis and x = a, x = b is ∫ab |f(x)| dx.
  • Use symmetry: for a circle or ellipse, find the first-quadrant area and multiply by 4.
  • Circle x² + y² = a²: area πa². Ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1: area πab.
  • Area between two curves: ∫ (upper − lower) dx between the points where they meet.
Example

Find the area bounded by y² = 9x, x = 2, x = 4 and the x-axis in the first quadrant.

∫24 3√x dx = 2[x3/2] from 2 to 4

= 2(8 − 2√2)

Answer: 16 − 4√2 sq units

Common mistakes

  • Leaving an area negative when the curve is below the axis.
  • Using πa² for an ellipse instead of πab.
  • Forgetting to double the area of a region that is symmetric about the x-axis.

faq.a: No. If the curve is below the axis, take the absolute value of the integral.

faq.q: Do I need to draw a sketch?
faq.a: Yes; it shows the limits and which curve is on top.
